info.title: Parro REST API (unofficial, read-only)
info.description:
Read-only description of the REST API behind **talk.parro.com**, the Dutch parent–school
communication app by Topicus (ParnasSys). The API is a Topicus *geon* API.
This spec was derived from the web client's traffic: a captured browser session and sanitized response
samples. Response schemas list **only fields seen in those samples**. Treat every object as
open: geon adds fields between contract versions. Every operation here was called at least once;
two paths from the web app's code, `/conversations` and `/timeslot`, answered `404` and are left out.

**A client for this API:** [parro-api-client](https://github.com/chris-swift-dev/parro-api-client),
a read-only command-line client and MCP server in plain Python
([download a release](https://github.com/chris-swift-dev/parro-api-client/releases/latest)).

Inspired by [fobatai/parro-mcp](https://github.com/fobatai/parro-mcp), a read-only MCP server for Parro
whose working login and API calls were the starting point for this specification.

## Conventions
* **Media type**: `Accept: application/vnd.topicus.geon+json;version=224`. The official client also
  sends the same value as `Content-Type`, even on GET. Responses sometimes omit `;version=…`.
* **Client headers**: `parro-app-version: web:2.27.0` and `parro-authorization-role: GUARDIAN:<guardianId>`.
  Derive the role from `GET /account/me`, which is called *without* the role header:
  the id is the `rel: self` link id of the first entry in `identity.guardians`.
* **Polymorphism**: every object carries a `dtype` (e.g. `event.RAnnouncementEventPrimer`). Several
  endpoints select the returned type with a `dtype` query parameter.
* **Ids** are 64-bit integers, found in `links[rel=self].id`. `href` values point at item resources
  (`/child/{id}`, `/group/{id}`, …) that are not described here.
* **Collections** come as `{"items": [...]}`. They are paged with `Range: items=<from>-<to>` and answer
  `206 Partial Content` with `Content-Range: items 0-1/2`, **even without a `Range` header**
  (the server's default page size is unknown). Add `topicus-Range-Count: Exact` to get an exact total.
* **Dates** are ISO-8601 with an offset. Fractional seconds vary from none to 3 digits.
* **CORS preflights** answer `Access-Control-Allow-Methods: DELETE, POST, GET, OPTIONS, PUT` on
  every path, even read-only ones such as `/child`. It is a server-wide setting and says nothing
  about which methods a path supports.

## Authentication
OAuth2 against the ParnasSys IdP (`https://inloggen.parnassys.net`, see the **Auth** operations).
The public client `MQygAaSBUcAgPU2WInKt` is pinned to the redirect URI `https://talk.parro.com/oauth2`.
There is no dynamic client registration or device grant, and loopback redirects are rejected.
* **Authorization code + PKCE (S256)**: browser login. Copy the `code` from the redirect URL quickly,
  because the web app also tries to redeem it and a code works only once.
* **Password grant**: `grant_type=password`, enabled for this client.
* A login lasts at most **8 hours**: the refresh token expires 8 hours after the login, also with scope
  `openid offline_access`, and a refresh returns a new refresh token with the same expiry (measured
  2026-11-06). The access token lasts 1 hour.
* The IdP **locks the account after a few failed logins**. Never retry a rejected password automatically.

## Attachments
Attachment entries carry a CloudFront `url`. It is **unsigned and needs no authentication**: anyone holding
it can download the file, so treat these URLs as secrets. Never send the Parro `Authorization` header to the CDN.
Document entries also carry `expiresAt`, exactly one year after the announcement in the sample. Whether the CDN
enforces it is unknown.
Announcements keep attachments in `attachments[]`; calendar items in `calendarItem.attachments[]`.
Choose the parser by `contentType`, not by the entry's `dtype`: a photo's SOURCE entry can be a
`RAttachmentDocumentEntry`.

## Trying it out
Paste an access token into **Authorize → bearerToken**. "Try it out" then works for the API operations,
including from a Swagger UI hosted on GitHub Pages: the API accepts cross-origin requests. The generated
curl commands include the token as well.

> ⚠️ **Logging in does not work from Swagger UI.** Leave the **parnassysOAuth** scheme and the **Auth**
> operations alone in the browser, and get the token outside it (see `/oauth2/token`):
> * *Authorization code*: the redirect URI is pinned to `https://talk.parro.com/oauth2`, so Swagger UI never
>   receives the code.
> * *Password*: the IdP answers `invalid_grant` for accounts it will not put through the password grant
>   (seen in practice), and cross-origin calls to the IdP are untested. **Every rejected attempt can count
>   toward the account lockout**, including the "Request body" variant, whose response the page may not
>   even be allowed to read.

## About this build
Public build: response and property examples taken from samples are left out.

get.summary: Announcements or calendar items of one group

206.description: A page of the collection (observed even without `Range`).

200.description: Same body as 206. Not observed for paged lists, but clients should accept it.

get.description:
The main feed. Query each group separately and merge by `sortDate`.

**Order: newest first.** For calendar items that means the *furthest future* first: in a live check (2026-11-05) a whole-school group's first 50 of 100 items lay 6 to 9 months ahead, so the coming weeks were on page 2. Page with `Range` until the dates reach today.

**Duplicates:** an announcement sent to several groups is returned once per group (same id; 2 of 71 events in that check). Merge by id.

**Multi-day calendar items come once per day**: each day is its own entry with its own event id, `dayNumber` (1..`numberOfDays`) and `sortDate`, all sharing one `calendarItem` (same id, `startDate`, `endDate`, `dayDates`). In that check one 40-day item gave 40 entries. Merge by `calendarItem` id.

`dtype` is required. Without it the API answers `406 EVENT_BAD_TYPE` (abstract supertype `RAbstractEvent`). **Pitfall:** `dtype=event.RAnnouncementEvent` answers **401**, not 406. Use `event.RAnnouncementEventPrimer` for announcements. A client that treats every 401 as an expired token will loop through logins.

get.summary: Personal iCalendar link for subscribing to the agenda
get.description:
Returns the account's personal **agenda subscription link** in `strings[0]`: `https://calendar.parro.com/ical/<calendarId>/<token>?noCache=<uuid>`. Calendar apps (Google, Apple, Outlook) subscribe to it and update by themselves; this is what the app's "sync the agenda" option copies.

⚠️ **The link is a secret**: anyone who has it can read the calendar, without logging in. Do not share or log it.

Checked live (2026-11-05):
* `calendarId` is none of the account, identity, guardian or organisation ids.
* The token stays the same across calls; only `noCache` changes. The link works without `noCache` (same content, same ETag).
* `GET` on the link needs no authentication and answers `200 text/calendar` (iCalendar with VTIMEZONE, `REFRESH-INTERVAL` and `X-PUBLISHED-TTL` of 1 hour). It holds the school year's items, each multi-day item once.

Not verified: ParnasSys lists agenda syncing as a feature of the paid *Parro Ouderapp*, so with *Parro Basis* this call may fail or return no link.

The same `calendar.RCalendarItem` that `GET /event/{id}` embeds as `calendarItem` (without `lastEditedBy`), addressed by the calendar item's own id.

Items of `type: VOLUNTEER` or `SCHOOLWIDE_VOLUNTEER` (seen live) ask for helpers: each entry in `resources[]` (`RCalendarItemVolunteerResource`) has a `title`, `amount` (helpers wanted), `amountCommitted`, `commitedByMe` (sic) and `commitments[]`. `numberOfTimeslots` and the `RCalendarItemTimeslotCreate` permission point to timeslots (e.g. parent–teacher talks) that hang off calendar items; their path is not known.

parameters.name: redirect_uri
parameters.description: Must be exactly the registered URI; loopback URIs are rejected (`invalid_client`).

parameters.name: scope
parameters.description: `openid`; `offline_access` is granted but does not lengthen the 8-hour login.

400.description: Invalid request, e.g. `invalid_client — Callback url does not match one of [registered]` for an unregistered `redirect_uri`.

post.description:
⚠️ **Not usable from Swagger UI.** Call it from a terminal or a client, and see the warning in the introduction.

**Two request shapes.**

* `authorization_code` and `refresh_token` send their parameters in the **query string** with an **empty body** and `Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded`, as the web client does.
* `password` sends a normal form-encoded **body** (`grant_type, client_id, username, password, scope`).

A wrong password answers `400 invalid_grant` and counts toward the account lockout. That same error also comes back for accounts the IdP will not put through the password grant. Clients then fall back to the HTML login form, once: `GET /oauth2/authorize` (PKCE, follow redirects, keep cookies) → POST `aanmelden=x&emailadres=…&wachtwoord=…` to the `signInForm` action without following the redirect → take `code` from `Location` → `authorization_code` exchange as above.

parameters.name: code
parameters.description: authorization_code: the code from the redirect.

post.summary: Revoke a refresh or access token (RFC 7009)

get.description: Advertised as `end_session_endpoint` in the discovery document; never called. Parameters follow OpenID Connect RP-Initiated Logout 1.0.
Location follows OIDC Discovery from `issuer`. Note: it also advertises `introspection_endpoint`, which needs client authentication and is not described.

bearerToken.description: Paste an access token. This is the only scheme usable from Swagger UI; "Try it out" works with it.

parnassysOAuth.description: ⚠️ **Documentation only: do not use it from Swagger UI.** The code flow cannot complete there, because the redirect URI is pinned to https://talk.parro.com/oauth2 and PKCE (S256) is required. The password flow is refused (`invalid_grant`) for some accounts, and each failed attempt can count toward the IdP's account lockout. Obtain a token outside the browser and use **bearerToken**.
